sections.label: Split
sections.description: A Hadamard on q0 splits the amplitude equally between indices 0 and 1. Each now has a 50% measurement probability.

sections.label: Double
sections.description: A Hadamard on q1 spreads the signal across indices 0–3. Each real amplitude is now 0.5, so each probability is 25%.

sections.label: Fill 32
sections.description: Hadamards on q2–q4 extend the flat real trace through index 31. The second half of the graph is still zero.

sections.label: Fill 64
sections.description: A Hadamard on q5 fills indices 32–63. All 64 points in the window now have real amplitude 1/8.

sections.label: Fill 2^50
sections.description: Hadamards on q6–q49 spread the signal across all 2^50 indices. The flat line now sits near 2.98e-8 on the vertical scale.
Z on q4 flips the real trace below zero at indices 16–31 and 48–63. Only the phase changes, so measurement probabilities stay equal.
A quarter-turn on q3 moves the amplitudes at indices 8–15 onto the imaginary axis. There the imaginary trace becomes positive and the real trace reaches zero.
An eighth-turn on q2 gives indices 4–7 equal positive real and imaginary parts. Each phase now spans four points.
A sixteenth-turn on q1 splits each four-point stretch into two pairs. Compare the imaginary amplitudes at indices 0 and 2.
The last rotation on q0 advances every odd index by 1/32 turn. The imaginary trace now forms a sine wave with a peak at 8, a zero at 16 and a trough at 24.
